Looking at the pieces on the triangular lattice, the hexagon consists of 24 small triangle units. Piece 2 has an area of 14 units and piece 3 has an area of 10 units, totaling 24.

Tracing the boundaries: piece 2's concave cut edge (the green zigzag path: down‑left, right, down‑right, left‑2, down‑right, down‑left) exactly matches piece 3's protruding boundary in reverse order. When piece 3 is slid into piece 2 along this interlocking edge, the outer edges complete all six sides of the regular hexagon.

Checking the other pairs: pieces 1 and 4 have matching areas (14+10) but their notch/protrusion sequences don't align (piece 1's cut edge cannot be filled by piece 4's shape), and pairs like 1&2 or 2&4 exceed the hexagon's area.

Only pieces 2 and 3 fit together perfectly to form the hexagon.
